newsitem.title: GERMANY: RWE plans to boost investment.
newsitem.headline: RWE plans to boost investment.

text.p: German diversified utility RWE AG said on Thursday that it hopes to strengthen its operations through further investment, both in domestic and foreign markets.
"In our home markets and markets abroad we are targeting acquisitions and possible cooperation," RWE management board chairman Dietmar Kuhnt said at the group's annual shareholders' meeting in Essen.

Even though the group was investing more money abroad of late, RWE remained one of Germany's biggest domestic investors, Kuhnt said. The telecommunications sector was one of the group's most important investment targets.

RWE spent a total of 7.2 billion marks ($4.7 billion) in the year to the end of June 1996 on investment and acquisitions, of which around 29 percent was invested abroad. Around half of the total investment went to the group's energy business.
After seeing high levels of investment in the previous year, RWE said it would be spending less on its waste disposal unit.
This was in counterpoint to the group's telecommunications sector, which would see high levels of growth. Kuhnt would not put a value on the increase in telecoms investment.
